links.outcome: Doctor decision quality with versus without LLM assistance, and LLM alone (accuracy, completeness)
links.effect: Completeness rose from 4.50 (doctors alone) to 4.90 with LLM support (p=0.0015 vs doctors; p=0.0010 vs LLMs alone); accuracy 4.50 to 4.67, not significant (p=0.19).
links.quote: Post hoc analysis demonstrated that doctors supported by LLMs achieved significantly higher completeness scores compared with both the doctors alone ( p = 0.0015) and the LLMs alone ( p = 0.0010).

links.outcome: Performance of clinicians using LLM in workflow versus standalone LLM or clinician alone
links.effect: LLM-assisted doctors had higher completeness (4.90) than doctors (4.50) or LLMs alone (4.60); accuracy trend 4.67 vs 4.50/4.48, p=0.19.
links.quote: Notably, when doctors made decisions with the support of LLMs, both accuracy (numerically) and completeness (significantly) improved.

links.outcome: Recognition of high-risk clinical scenario (invasive pulmonary aspergillosis after influenza)
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 omitted invasive pulmonary aspergillosis from top three differentials; Grok 3 advised against antifungal treatment even after supporting evidence was provided.
links.quote: In this study, several models did not promptly recognize the elevated risk of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in patients with influenza, leading to diagnostic errors and delayed antifungal recommendations.

links.outcome: Completeness and prioritization of serious conditions in LLM differential diagnoses
links.effect: In Case 1, top three differentials from DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 did not include invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, a serious condition.
links.quote: In Case 1 ( Supplementary Table 1 in Supplementary material 2 ), which involved a patient with post-influenza pneumonia and a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the top three differential diagnoses generated by DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 did not include invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

links.outcome: LLM versus infectious disease resident performance on exam questions
links.effect: LLMs comparable to doctors on low-order questions (87.4-92.3% vs 88.4%, p=0.54); doctors had higher high-order score rate (76.5% vs 54.5-66.5%, p=0.10).
links.quote: Doctors achieved the highest score rate (164.5/215, 76.5%), with numerically higher performance than all LLMs.

unlisted_practices: Incorporating region-specific training data and local guidelines to improve LLM performance for regionally prevalent diseases (tuberculosis errors higher in Western-trained models)

links.outcome: physician decision completeness with LLM support
links.effect: Completeness rose from 4.50 to 4.90 (8.89% improvement); group difference p=0.0006.
links.quote: Human–AI collaboration raised doctors’ overall completeness score from 4.50 to 4.90, corresponding to an 8.89% improvement.

links.outcome: LLM versus doctors on high-order exam questions
links.quote: Doctors achieved the highest score rate (164.5/215, 76.5%), with numerically higher performance than all LLMs.

links.outcome: standalone LLM missed serious differential diagnosis
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 top three differentials omitted invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in Case 1.
links.quote: In Case 1 ( Supplementary Table 1 in Supplementary material 2 ), which involved a patient with post-influenza pneumonia and a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the top three differential diagnoses generated by DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 did not include invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

links.outcome: incorrect treatment recommendation despite diagnostic evidence
links.effect: After Aspergillus IgG 500.00 AU/mL and BALF NGS read count 12, Grok 3 said immediate voriconazole was unnecessary.
links.quote: More concerningly, even after additional diagnostic evidence was provided—including a markedly elevated Aspergillus IgG level (500.00 AU/mL, normal range <120 AU/mL) and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid Next-Generation Sequencing detecting Aspergillus fumigatus sequences (read count: 12)—Grok 3 still responded: “Elevated IgG and NGS sequences suggest possible colonization or chronic infection, but negative GM and low sequence numbers make immediate antifungal treatment (e.g., voriconazole) unnecessary unless clinical worsening or CT findings (e.g., cavities) suggest CPA.”

links.outcome: regional disease prevalence error pattern
links.effect: TB errors exceeded 60% for Gemini 14/21 (66.7%), ChatGPT-5 17/26 (65.4%), and Grok 3 16/25 (64.0%); DeepSeek 7/16 (43.8%).
links.quote: Except for DeepSeek-R1 (7/16, 43.8%) and doctors (12/24, 50.0%), tuberculosis-related errors exceeded 60% of total errors in most LLMs trained primarily on Western corpora, including Gemini 2.5 Flash (14/21, 66.7%), ChatGPT-5 (17/26, 65.4%), and Grok 3 (16/25, 64.0%) ( Figure 2 ; Supplementary Table 12 in Supplementary material 5 ).
